Berkeley Warns Pretax Profit Will Be First-Half Weighted as Buyers Hold Off
Berkeley Group said it expects pretax profit for the year to be weighted toward its fiscal first half as some buyers hold off due to political uncertainty.
The London-listed home builder said some buyers might defer transactions until after the U.K. government outlines its budget at the end of October, and any election uncertainty dissipates.

Continuing political uncertainty and the prolonged Middle East conflict have worsened the economy and consumer confidence, slowing down general trading and housing market activity, Berkeley said Friday.
In March, the company said it expected pretax profit for the year ending April 2027 to be similar to that seen in fiscal 2026, when it reported pretax profit of 451.4 million pounds ($609.8 million).
Still, Berkeley said it continued to operate within its four-year 1.4 billion pounds pretax profit plan.

Net cash at the half year point will be around 250 million pounds and reflect the level of shareholder returns along with investment in the core business and the Build to Rent platform, the company said.

"While Berkeley is receiving good and stable levels of inquiries, the uncertainty and volatility in the market means that customers without an immediate need to move and readily available liquidity remain more cautious to commit," it said.
